about: Design section 7.1's dependency gate (B4 recheck 6 item 2; rebuilt for the B7 milestone 2
break-it and its three rechecks). It fails closed on review, not on detection. For builds
made through the supported entry point, scripts/build.sh with a profile below in its closed
compiler environment, it guarantees two things: no unreviewed package enters the build, and
every occurrence of a curated destructive sink identifier, and every trait impl or type
alias on std's and Tokio's file and process types, in the checked-in source of the runtime
subtree of a package declared non-destructive is flagged for review. A raw cargo build with
other feature or compiler flags is outside the guarantee. Deciding whether an API is
destructive is the reviewer's job; the gate is not a proof. `profiles` lists every
supported build: the workspace features (member/feature) scripts/build.sh passes, with
--locked, and nothing else; it refuses --features, -F, --all-features,
--no-default-features, --manifest-path, --config, -Z and a clippy argument tail, and
refuses ambient compiler flags and wrappers (RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS, RUSTC_WRAPPER
and the rest), setting empty ones itself so no Cargo config file supplies any; every
workspace build script refuses a --cfg, -Z or response-file flag. The gate runs cargo
metadata --locked with exactly each profile's flags: a profile may name only a declared
workspace feature, and every package a profile resolves must be locked and reviewed.
`packages` has an entry for every package in Cargo.lock outside the workspace, keyed
name@version and pinned to its Cargo.lock `checksum` and the `features` the profiles
resolve (their union); one name@version from two sources is refused outright. Each has its
`kind` (runtime, build-only or dev-only, from the manifests for a direct dependency and the
union of the profiles' graphs otherwise), its `capability` (`none`, or a set of filesystem,
process, signals, syscalls, network) and a justification (`why`, or a `group` from
`groups`, allowed only for `none` packages whose source names no std::fs, std::process,
std::os fs/fd/process, libc or tokio::fs/process path at all). A new package, version,
checksum or feature set fails until reviewed; scripts/dependency-gate-review.py drafts the
mechanical fields. A direct dependency with a destructive-capable category lists its
`destructive` paths, each disallowed in clippy.toml, or records `no_destructive_api`; a
`none` package over a raw system-call crate records `raw_use`. For every `none`, `network`
or `no_destructive_api` package in the runtime graph (or direct), the checked-in source of
its whole runtime subtree is scanned: every .rs file under each package's root (build
scripts and binaries included; unreached tests/, benches/ and examples/ files excepted),
and every file a literal #[path] or include! edge reaches. An edge outside the package
root refuses it; an edge the loader cannot follow is an `unresolved source edge` hit;
generated OUT_DIR code is not read. The scan flags the curated sink identifiers wherever
they occur (method calls, UFCS, function values, use lists, definitions), paths clippy.toml
disallows, trait impls on std's and Tokio's file and process types (through use and type
aliases) and type aliases of them; each hit needs a `sink_exceptions` entry scoped to that
package, version and feature set, with why. proven::tests::dependency_gate checks all of
it; section 7.1 has the model and its limits.

default.why: the release build scripts/install.sh installs (and so scripts/upgrade.sh's binaries), the default CI jobs' tests, clippy and release build, and the library tests the VM scripts build

firecracker-test-deployment.why: Phase 1b B6's isolated Firecracker test deployment: CI's feature job (tests, clippy, the feature build) and the daemon and client scripts/b4-vm-tests.sh builds

groups.pure-computation: Pure computation: in-memory data structures, parsing, encoding, hashing, formatting, type-level code and async plumbing (futures, wakers, channels, pin projection). It opens, removes, renames, truncates and runs nothing and makes no raw system call: the gate checks that its library source names no std::fs, std::process, std::os fs, fd or process extension, libc or tokio::fs/process path at all, and that no raw system-call crate is under it.
groups.compile-time: Build-time code generation: a procedural macro, or a library only procedural macros and code generators use (token streams, Rust syntax trees, pretty-printing). It runs in the compiler or a build script on the source it is given and is never linked into a kilnd binary; the gate checks its library source names no std::fs, std::process, std::os fs, fd or process extension, libc or tokio::fs/process path at all.

anstream@1.0.0.why: clap's styled output: writes ANSI-styled text to the stream it is given (stdout, stderr, or a File the caller passes, hence its writer impls for std::fs::File) and strips styles when that stream is not a terminal; it opens, removes or renames nothing

anstyle-query@1.1.5.raw_use: Windows console mode query (GetConsoleMode/SetConsoleMode on the process's own console) through windows-sys, on Windows only; elsewhere it reads TERM, COLORTERM, NO_COLOR and CLICOLOR
anstyle-query@1.1.5.why: clap's terminal colour detection from environment variables

anstyle-wincon@3.0.11.raw_use: Windows console text attributes (SetConsoleTextAttribute) through windows-sys
anstyle-wincon@3.0.11.why: styling for legacy Windows consoles (anstream's wincon feature); Windows only: never compiled for kilnd's Linux helper or its macOS development builds. Its stream impl for std::fs::File writes to a file it is given

anyhow@1.0.104.why: error values and context chains: carries and formats errors in memory; no file, process or system-call API

bytes@1.12.1.why: byte buffers (Bytes, BytesMut): in-memory only; its one std::process path is std::process::abort on a reference-count overflow, ending this process

cc@1.8.0.why: build-time only, for libsqlite3-sys's build script: runs the C compiler and archiver and writes object files and the archive under OUT_DIR on the build host; never linked into kilnd

clap@4.6.7.why: argument parsing: reads the arguments and environment it is given and prints help

clap_builder@4.6.7.why: clap's argument parser: reads the arguments and environment it is given, prints help and errors, and on a parse error ends this process (std::process::exit); its own clap::Command type is not std::process::Command

cpufeatures@0.2.17.raw_use: libc::getauxval (Linux) and libc::sysctlbyname (macOS) to read CPU feature flags, nothing else

errno@0.3.14.raw_use: libc's errno location, to read and set this thread's errno
errno@0.3.14.why: rustix's portable errno access (tempfile, build and test only) and signal-hook-registry's

find-msvc-tools@0.1.14.why: build-time only, for cc on Windows: finds the MSVC toolchain through the registry and vswhere.exe; Windows only: never compiled for kilnd's Linux helper or its macOS development builds

getrandom@0.4.3.raw_use: getrandom(2)/getentropy(2) through libc for random bytes, nothing else
getrandom@0.4.3.why: build-time and test only (tempfile's random names, through fastrand's seed on some targets)

h2@0.4.20.why: raw HTTP/2 clients in admission tests; also linked through tonic, whose transport it is

hashbrown@0.17.1.why: SwissTable hash maps, in memory (indexmap's backing table). Its only libc use is mmap/munmap in its own map.rs test allocator, compiled only for its tests: hashbrown has no libc dependency

httparse@1.10.1.why: HTTP/1 request and response parsing in memory (hyper's). Its library opens, removes and runs nothing; its build script (build-time only) runs `rustc --version` to choose SIMD cfgs, so the whole-package scan (recheck 3) no longer lets it share pure-computation.

hyper-timeout@0.5.2.why: tonic's client connector with connect/read/write timeouts over hyper and Tokio's sockets; kilnd uses tonic only over its Unix socket

hyper-util@0.1.21.why: TokioIo adapters for the Unix-socket transport; its libc use is socket options, with no file, signal or subprocess API

hyper@1.12.0.why: HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 over the transport tonic and hyper-util give it (Tokio sockets): parses and writes frames on that connection; no file or process API. Its one std::process path is std::process::abort in its C FFI layer, not compiled without hyper's ffi cfg

is_terminal_polyfill@1.70.2.why: an IsTerminal trait for older toolchains, implemented for std::fs::File, the standard streams and descriptors: asks whether a descriptor is a terminal and nothing else

libc@0.2.190.why: the raw system-call surface: every destructive function (every_destructive_libc_function_is_disallowed checks the locked source) is in clippy.toml, reachable only from the approved modules

libsqlite3-sys@0.35.0.why: rusqlite's bundled SQLite: the C library compiled by its build script (cc), with Rust bindings only. SQLite opens and writes the database file rusqlite gives it and creates, truncates and unlinks that database's own -journal, -wal and -shm files (design 7.1); kilnd's code never names this crate

linux-raw-sys@0.12.1.why: Linux UAPI constants and structs for rustix; build-time and test only (tempfile, through prost-build and kilnd's dev-dependencies), never linked into kilnd

mio@1.2.4.why: Tokio's event loop: epoll/kqueue registration, sockets, pipes and the waker (an eventfd or pipe it creates itself). Its libc::ioctl is FIONBIO, setting O_NONBLOCK on a pipe it owns

nu-ansi-term@0.50.3.raw_use: enables ANSI processing on the Windows console (SetConsoleMode) through windows-sys, on Windows only
nu-ansi-term@0.50.3.why: tracing-subscriber's ANSI colours for its log lines

pkg-config@0.3.34.why: build-time only, for libsqlite3-sys's build script: runs pkg-config on the build host (unused with the bundled feature); never linked into kilnd

prettyplease@0.2.37.why: Pretty-prints generated Rust syntax trees for prost-build and tonic-prost-build at build time; never linked into a kilnd binary. Its build script only checks the compiler version and exits (process::exit) on an unsupported one, so the whole-package scan (recheck 3) no longer lets it share compile-time.

proc-macro2@1.0.107.why: Token streams for procedural macros and code generators, at build time; never linked into a kilnd binary. Its build script runs rustc in a probe directory under OUT_DIR, which it creates and removes, so the whole-package scan (recheck 3) no longer lets it share compile-time.

prost-build@0.14.4.why: build-time only, under tonic-prost-build in kilnd-api's build script: runs protoc, writes the generated Rust into OUT_DIR and uses a tempfile scratch directory on the build host; never linked into kilnd

prost@0.14.4.why: protobuf message encoding and decoding over in-memory buffers

pulldown-cmark@0.13.4.why: Markdown parsing for prost-build's generated doc comments, at build time; never linked into a kilnd binary. Its build script (spec-test generation, its gen-tests feature, not enabled) and its command-line binary (src/main.rs, not built as a dependency) open files, so the whole-package scan (recheck 3) no longer lets it share pure-computation.

quote@1.0.47.why: Quasi-quoting for procedural macros and code generators, at build time; never linked into a kilnd binary. Its build script runs `rustc --version`, so the whole-package scan (recheck 3) no longer lets it share compile-time.

r-efi@6.0.0.why: UEFI protocol type definitions for getrandom's UEFI backend; build-time only and never compiled for Linux or macOS

rusqlite@0.37.0.no_destructive_api: with the enabled features (bundled, functions) its API opens and writes the database it is given by path and has no removal, rename, truncation or copy function; SQLite's own -wal/-shm/-journal maintenance is the one dependency-internal unlink (design 7.1)
rusqlite@0.37.0.why: SQLite through bundled libsqlite3-sys, for kilnd's own database

rustix@1.1.5.why: tempfile's system calls (create, write and remove its own temporary files and directories); build-time (prost-build's scratch directory) and test only, never linked into kilnd

serde@1.0.229.why: serialization traits and their derives (serde_derive runs at build time); in memory

serde_json@1.0.154.why: JSON encoding and decoding over buffers and the readers and writers it is given; opens nothing

sha2@0.10.9.why: SHA-256 over the bytes it is given (cpufeatures underneath only reads CPU feature flags)

signal-hook-registry@1.4.8.why: Tokio's signal module: installs signal handlers with sigaction and forwards deliveries to Tokio; it sends no signal to another process (its libc::raise calls re-raise to this process when emulating a default handler)

socket2@0.6.5.why: socket options and creation for Tokio and hyper-util (setsockopt, SO_* and the like) on sockets they own

tempfile@3.27.0.why: test scratch directories; TempDir removes only its own on drop. Never a normal dependency

thiserror@2.0.21.why: error-type derives (thiserror-impl is the build-time macro); at runtime only the Display and Error impls it generates

tokio-stream@0.1.19.why: Stream adapters over Tokio types (its net feature wraps listeners kilnd already owns); no file, signal or subprocess API

tokio-util@0.7.20.raw_use: libc::memchr only, for its codec's delimiter search
tokio-util@0.7.20.why: CancellationToken and task trackers; no file, signal or subprocess API

tracing@0.1.44.why: structured logging macros and spans, dispatched to the installed subscriber

WinconStream for std::fs::File writes styled text to a file it is given; Windows console attributes otherwise. Windows only.
String::truncate trimming a formatted backtrace: in-memory length changes on its own buffers (Vec, String, BytesMut, SmallVec and the like), not File::set_len or OpenOptions::truncate.

exec is its executor plumbing: the common::exec module, Exec type and `exec` fields holding the caller's task executor (and the rt-tracing-exec-force feature name in cfg attributes); it spawns futures, never a program.
Vec::set_len and truncate on the map's own entry vector: in-memory length changes on its own buffers (Vec, String, BytesMut, SmallVec and the like), not File::set_len or OpenOptions::truncate.

libc's own declarations of the C functions (extern fn kill, rename, truncate, umount, umount2, unlink, unlinkat, unmount, Haiku's send_signal), a struct field named copy (Apple) and solarish siginfo accessors' `kill` bindings. libc is reviewed with its destructive capabilities, and clippy.toml disallows each destructive function for workspace code; a package declared non-destructive that calls one names it in its own source, where this scan flags it.

The crate_root! macro's docs.rs-only `cfg_attr(all(docsrs, if_docsrs_then_no_serde_core), path = "core/...")`, serde's facade layout (serde ships src/core and the gate follows these there). serde_core ships no src/core, so a build with that cfg could not compile, and no supported build sets it; every checked-in .rs file under serde_core is scanned whatever these paths would name.

Vec::set_len after writing escaped UTF-8 into its scratch buffer and String::truncate on an error message: in-memory length changes on its own buffers (Vec, String, BytesMut, SmallVec and the like), not File::set_len or OpenOptions::truncate. copy is a macro metavariable ($copy:tt) in json!.

SmallVec's own set_len and truncate, and Vec::set_len when it spills: in-memory length changes on its own buffers (Vec, String, BytesMut, SmallVec and the like), not File::set_len or OpenOptions::truncate. copy is core::ptr::copy shifting elements inside its own buffer.

build.rs only (recheck 3's whole-package scan reads build scripts too): it runs on the build host at compile time and is never linked into a kilnd binary. It writes its generated OUT_DIR/private.rs (fs::write), runs the rustc cargo names to probe for std backtrace support (Command::new), then removes its own probe directory, OUT_DIR/probe (fs::remove_dir_all).

Tokio's own implementation of the API its entry declares (filesystem, process, signals): tokio::fs wraps std::fs::{copy, remove_dir, remove_dir_all, remove_file, rename, write} and File::set_len/OpenOptions::truncate, tokio::process wraps std::process::Command, Child::kill (and its pidfd reaper's libc::syscall pidfd_open), and Vec::set_len/truncate appear in its I/O buffers. Each of those Tokio paths is disallowed in clippy.toml, so workspace code reaches none of them outside the approved modules; the impls are Tokio's own wrappers for std's OpenOptions and Child. The identifier scan also sees tokio::fs's own copy, remove_dir, remove_dir_all, remove_file and rename (definitions and re-exports of the wrappers above, each disallowed in clippy.toml as tokio::fs::...), its io-uring rename op, tokio::io::copy (stream to writer), and `exec` as the name of a runtime scheduler binding.
BytesMut::truncate dropping a codec's delimiter byte: in-memory length changes on its own buffers (Vec, String, BytesMut, SmallVec and the like), not File::set_len or OpenOptions::truncate.

copy is std::io::copy streaming a gRPC message through a (de)compressor into its output buffer (codec/compression.rs, behind compression features kilnd does not enable); exec is the executor a channel spawns its connection futures on.

MakeWriter for std::fs::File lets a subscriber write log lines to a file the caller opened; kilnd's subscriber writes to stderr. It writes, never sets a length, removes or renames. Its associated type Writer = &'a std::fs::File is that impl's writer.

Win32 binding declarations: parameters and fields named copy, persist and persistentlogininfo in its link! externs and structs. It is a Windows-only dependency kilnd never builds for; its own capability is reviewed separately.
core::ptr::copy shifting digits inside its own float-formatting buffer.
